subject: Planned subprocessor swap — export path attestation and escrow evidence

Date: 2027-05-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Heads-up: planned subprocessor swap + export path question

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the call yesterday. As we discussed, FinRoute has a regulatory review next month and we need a concise attestation of any planned subprocessor changes that could affect cross-border export controls or encryption key custody for our EU/US customer flows. Specifically: 

- Is Redwood planning to add or swap any telemetry/telemetry-proxy processors in the next 90 days?
- If a swap is planned, can you provide the expected export path (country-by-country) and whether keys remain under KMS in the US?

We’d like to include an excerpt in our regulator briefing. If you can attach the current roster and any draft DPA addendum, that’d be very helpful.

Best,
Allen
Head of Platform Ops | FinRoute Payments

Irene / Kim — Allen at FinRoute needs a crisp attestation for regulators about a potential subprocessor swap and whether export paths / key custody change. Key asks from Allen: roster, country-by-country export path, and confirmation on KMS custody.

Can you confirm: 
1) Any scheduled provider decommissions or replacements in telemetry/telemetry-proxy within the next 90 days?
2) If we do a swap, which countries would see egress, and do any of the candidate providers require keys to be moved out of our US-managed KMS?
3) If there is an exposure, can we provide a mitigator with an escrow/onshore fallback and a short timeline for evidence?

I’m looping in FinRoute for transparency. I’m happy to draft the attestation once you give bullets. Thanks.

— Jasmine
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Allen Baker <allen.baker@finroute.com>, legal@finroute.com
Date: 2027-05-20T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Heads-up: planned subprocessor swap + export path question

Jasmine — quick summary after sync with infra and the vendor team: 

- Planned change: a phased swap of one telemetry relay vendor (edge-collector) from RelayFast -> StreamBridge. This is scheduled as a background deployment with a canary window starting 2027-07-02; the full rollout depends on performance and legal signoff.
- Export path: both RelayFast and StreamBridge operate EU nodes; egress for EU-origin requests stays within the EU for processing; however, telemetry metadata (non-customer payload) is replicated to our US analytics cluster for platform monitoring. The replication pipeline is encrypted in transit and at rest.
- KMS custody: candidate StreamBridge supports envelope encryption; Redwood will continue to hold root keys in our US KMS. StreamBridge will only receive encrypted blobs and will not have plaintext key material.
- Escrow/onshore fallback: Infra has prepared an escrow plan — if StreamBridge requires temporary elevated access we can route EU telemetry through our onshore fallback (EdgeGate) for up to 30 days. Evidence artifacts available: connectivity maps and an evidence packet we can share.

I’ll attach a current roster and the draft DPA addendum for FinRoute review; Kim, please confirm legal redlines.

Irene
Head of Infrastructure Compliance | Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessor_roster_v3.xlsx (roster, country columns, encryption notes)
Attachment: dpa_addendum_draft_for_review.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Allen Baker <allen.baker@finroute.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned subprocessor swap — export path attestation and escrow evidence

Allen — thanks for the patient turnaround. Attestation below for your regulator packet; attached are the signed DPA addendum (redwood side) and a sanitized roster slice for regulator review.

Attestation (for FinRoute):
- Redwood currently plans a phased vendor swap for one telemetry relay provider (planned canary: 2027-07-02).
- Data residency impact: No customer payload will be exported outside jurisdictions specified in the current DPA. Telemetry metadata used for platform analytics may be replicated to Redwood-managed analytics clusters in the United States; these artifacts are encrypted in transit and at rest.
- Key custody: Root keys remain in Redwood-managed US KMS. Candidate providers will only process encrypted blobs and will not receive plaintext keys or root key material.
- Escrow / fallback: Redwood confirms an onshore fallback routing (EdgeGate) is available for a 30-day window to meet urgent regulator requirements; evidence packet includes routing diagrams and the short-term control checklist.

Attachments: dpa_addendum_finroute_signed.pdf; subprocessor_roster_v3.xlsx

Next steps we propose: 
1) FinRoute legal to confirm whether the attestation text is sufficient for the regulator.
2) If regulator requests additional artifacts, Redwood can provide connectivity maps and a signed control checklist under NDA.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
